title: Machine learning prioritizes C16orf74 as an EMT regulator in head and neck cancer
summary: After single-cell RNA sequencing identified a malignant EMT epithelial subpopulation in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, an ensemble of six machine learning algorithms ranked 13 candidate genes and prioritized C16orf74. Gain- and loss-of-function assays in cells confirmed effects on EMT, migration, invasion and tumor-sphere formation, and a pathomics prognostic model was built from H&E slides, with an external CPTAC-HNSCC cohort. Validation of the gene is in vitro only, the ML ranked pre-filtered candidates, and prognostic findings are retrospective.
ai_technology: Ensemble of six ML algorithms (SVM, random forest, GBM, GLM, LASSO, neural network) ranking EMT-associated candidate genes

evidence.tested: Gain- and loss-of-function wet-lab assays in HNSCC cells; external CPTAC-HNSCC cohort for the prognostic model.
evidence.unknown: Role of C16orf74 in patients and the HMGA2 mechanism remain candidate findings; no clinical testing.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked pre-filtered candidate genes by importance to prioritize C16orf74.
